newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks pinned down by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks pinned down by profit-taking.

text.p: The Australian share market closed weaker on Wednesday after a slide in bank issues prompted investors to take profits across the board after the market's strong performance over the past few weeks.

The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, finished 21 points lower at 2,310.7, not far off its intra-day low of 2,309.3. The December share price index ended 27 points down at 2,332, a 22.7 point premium to the index.
Brokers said profit-taking in the bank sector was triggered by less than encouraging comments made by the Commonwealth's chairman at the bank's annual meeting in Melbourne on Tuesday.
The big bank's fortunes were also tied to local interest rates as their yields would become even more attractive to investors if there was another rate cut, dealers said.
"The pull-back gained momentum over the afternoon with resource issues hit as hard as industrials, even though metal prices were a bit better last night," one Brisbane dealer said.

Today's pull-back was judged by brokers as healthy reaction to recent gains with underlying sentiment still seen positive. Transport group Brambles Industries, which went ex-dividend today, also was contributed to market weakness. Brambles paid a final dividend of 35 cents.

Takeover target TNT was active later in the session with dealers saying institutions were active buyers on the news that large TNT shareholder, investment bank Bankers Trust may hold out for a higher price from TNT's Dutch suitor, KPN.
Dealers also said that KPN was rumoured to be considering lifting its bid for TNT if it did not recieve enough acceptances.

The shares of life office National Mutual were also active following the group's strong debut on Tuesday. National Mutual stock ended slightly weaker, pulling back from the highs it reached near the close on Tuesday.

In other markets, Australian bonds remained lower after U.S. markets fell on Tuesday. At 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the yield on 10-year T-bonds were at 7.63 percent, 0.02 percent above Tuesday's closing levels.
The Australian dollar was fighting to hold gains forced by exporter and samurai-linked demand on Tuesday. At 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the currency was quoted at US$0.7895/00.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trade was steady as investors factored in the market's late pull-back.
